new_scholarship.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) funds international students who will study at Japanese national universities as undergraduates. MEXT publishes the terms in the FY2027 Application Guidelines and the application is made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general, or through a university recommendation. The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition at the accepting university and provides round-trip airfare. Under embassy recommendation the scholarship runs for five years including one year of Japanese language training.

programme_detail_official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) is one of seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship programme, awarded by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology of Japan to international students admitted to Japanese national universities. Applicants are selected either by embassy recommendation or by university recommendation. Under embassy recommendation the award covers a monthly scholarship, tuition and round-trip airfare for five years including one year of Japanese language training.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme
programme_detail_official.coverage: Monthly scholarship of JPY 117,000, tuition exemption at the accepting national university, and round-trip airfare under embassy recommendation

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your age band: applicants must in principle have been born on or after 2 April 2002
Confirm you hold the nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan and that you are not a Japanese national
Ask your Japanese embassy or consulate general for its own application deadline and examination dates - they are not published centrally
Prepare two identical packets (originals and copies) with document numbers 1 to 9 written on each first page
Obtain a medical certificate completed and signed by a physician
Decide your field of study, course and up to three majors from the official table
If you want direct placement, plan to contact universities for a letter of provisional acceptance using the MEXT-specified format only
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy deadline, which is set locally and differs by country
Submitting only one packet instead of an original set plus a copy set
Untranslated documents, or documents not in Japanese or English
Choosing a field, course or major combination that does not exist in the official table
Failing the written academic examination or interview
Not declaring a previous MEXT scholarship award, which makes the applicant ineligible
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses beyond the monthly scholarship, in the preparatory year and beyond
Airfares other than the single round-trip ticket provided
Accommodation costs not covered by the university
All expenses of accompanying family members
document_audit: Application Form for FY2027, not an older year's form

Academic transcripts showing the grade scale applied, with follow-up transcripts after graduation
Certificate of graduation or prospective graduation matched to the applicant's current level
Recommendation letter from the president, dean or academic advisor
Medical certificate in the prescribed MEXT format, signed and dated by a physician
Language proficiency certificate issued within two years of the application date, if held

You must be able to arrive in Japan between 1 April and 7 April 2027; personal delay means travel expenses are not paid.

Contact the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country for the local deadline and written examination date

Collect transcripts, graduation or prospective graduation certificates and the recommendation letter
Assemble one packet of originals and one of copies, numbering documents 1 to 9
Submit to the diplomatic mission before its deadline and track down the first screening result
After the first screening, contact universities for a provisional acceptance letter in the MEXT format

new_scholarship.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students) funds international undergraduates who major in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year at designated Japanese universities. Applicants must already have studied Japanese studies for at least one year and must remain enrolled at their home institution on return. MEXT states that it "offers scholarships to international students who wish to study for a period of one year at designated Japanese universities as Japanese Studies Students". The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition and provides round-trip airfare.

programme_detail_official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students) is one of seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship programme. It funds international undergraduates majoring in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year on a designated Japanese Studies Program course at a Japanese university. The official MEXT types table places Japanese studies students at undergraduate level with a JPY 117,000 monthly scholarship, tuition exemption and round-trip airfare. Applications go to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's country.

You must arrive within two weeks before the course start date, usually September or October; personal delay means travel expenses are not paid.
The official guidelines state that extension of the scholarship period is not permitted, and scholarship payment can start a month later than the enrolment date if the semester begins mid-month.

Number documents 1 to 8 and submit to the diplomatic mission

new_scholarship.description: The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard Program) let excellent postdoctoral researchers from other countries conduct cooperative research in Japan with a Japanese host researcher. JSPS runs two open-call rounds a year and awarded 120 fellowships in each FY2027 round. The fellowship pays a maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance. Applications are submitted by the host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System, not by candidates directly.

programme_detail_official.description: The Standard Program of the Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan is JSPS's open-call route for excellent postdoctoral researchers from other countries to conduct cooperative research with a Japanese host researcher. JSPS publishes two rounds a year with a fixed deadline of 5 p.m. JST, and 120 fellowships are awarded in each FY2027 round. Financial support comprises a maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Monthly maintenance allowance, round-trip airfare, settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance; no tuition element

application_readiness_checklist: Find a Japanese host researcher who agrees to submit the application, since candidates cannot apply directly
Confirm you hold, or will receive, a doctoral degree before the fellowship start date
Note that the FY2027 1st round closed on 28 August 2026; target the 2nd round deadline of 23 April 2027 at 5 p.m. JST
Agree the intended arrival window with your host: 1 September to 30 November 2027 for the 2nd round
Budget 12 to 24 months in full month units and plan research equipment costs, which the fellowship does not cover
Do not buy air tickets yourself; book through the travel agency designated by JSPS
common_rejection_risks: No Japanese host researcher willing to submit the nomination
Missing the 5 p.m. JST deadline for the round
Not holding a doctoral degree, or unable to document an imminent one
Applying for a duration outside 12 to 24 months or not in whole months
Being a Japanese national or permanent resident of Japan
Bought air tickets independently, which JSPS will not reimburse
estimated_uncovered_costs: Research equipment, consumables and computing costs not covered by a separate Grant-in-Aid
Health insurance beyond the JSPS-provided overseas travel insurance
Living costs above the JPY 362,000 monthly allowance
Airfare beyond the single round-trip economy ticket issued under JSPS regulations
document_audit: JSPS Electronic Application System submission made by the host researcher, timestamped before the deadline

alerts.message: Only two open-call rounds exist per fiscal year with exactly 120 fellowships each; the next deadline after 2026-10-04 is 23 April 2027 at 5 p.m. JST.
The 2nd round accepts arrival in Japan between 1 September and 30 November 2027; results are published in early August 2027.
If you were already living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date, the outbound airfare and the settling-in allowance are not paid.
JSPS marks the Strategic Program as 'Offering was ended'; do not treat it as an open route.

research_notes.logo: The fellowship schedule page has no logo asset matching /logo/i and its og:image is the generic 122,158 B site banner /assets/a/images/common/og.jpg, which is a page banner rather than the JSPS mark. JSPS publishes a dedicated logo page at https://www.jsps.go.jp/english/e-organization/logo/ (page title 'JSPS Logo | Organization | Japan Society for the Promotion of Science'). Its header asset https://www.jsps.go.jp/assets/a/images/common/ttl-en.svg probed 200 image/svg+xml at 37,458 bytes with a single fill #39427b and no white, so it is safe on a light card. The same logo page also publishes https://www.jsps.go.jp/file/cms/60001/4760/image.png?updated=20240327_093633 (200 image/png, 82,087 B, 1532x315, alt '日本学術振興会ロゴ'), which pixel analysis on a white canvas shows at 7.0% dark versus 91.6% light pixels, so it is also usable as a fallback. Rejected the favicon.ico (4,286 B) and favicon.png (5,332 B) as too small to be a legible wordmark.
